question.text: Satpura Market-Neutral Fund (a Cat III AIF) is computing its tax withholding on derivatives income before passing returns to investors. Per Section 2.6.1, which statement correctly characterises the tax position of an India-based Cat III AIF relative to offshore hedge funds?

answer.text: Cat III income is fully tax-exempt; offshore hedge funds face higher tax
Cat III income is taxed via PASS-THROUGH to investors under Section 115UB, with 10% TDS under Section 194LBB

Cat III income is taxed AT THE FUND LEVEL, requiring the fund to withhold 42.7% of all derivatives income before distributing to investors - giving offshore hedge funds a comparative tax advantage in several jurisdictions
Cat III is taxed like a listed equity mutual fund at 10% LTCG flat

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.6.1 states: "The income of Category III AIFs are taxed at fund level, requiring the fund to withhold 42.7 per cent of all income on derivatives trading before they pass on the returns to investors." Offshore jurisdictions often provide more favourable treatment, which is why offshore hedge funds enjoy a comparative tax advantage. Category III is specifically excluded from the Category I/II pass-through regime (pp. 365-367, 373-374). The Trap: Option A is fictitious. Option B is the Category I/II pass-through treatment (Section 115UB and Section 194LBB) - a classic Cat I/II vs Cat III swap trap. Option D applies a mutual-fund rate to an AIF incorrectly. Note: The 42.7% fund-level withholding is the direct workbook figure. Risk-return benchmarking should rely on sourced metrics; GIFT-IFSC or Section 80LA tax-holiday claims are not supported by the checked workbook pages and should not be inferred.
